blocks.en: ✨ Worship — Unit 2: Characteristics & Importance of Worship
blocks.es_reference: ✨ Adoración — Unidad 2: Características e Importancia de la Adoración

blocks.en: Chapala Theological Seminary, a ministry of Common Ground Fellowship | Professor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers
blocks.es_reference: Seminario Teológico de Chapala, un ministerio de Common Ground Fellowship | Profesor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers

blocks.en: This course is drawn from the worship curriculum of Dr. Wayne Cook, who served eleven years as Professor of Pastoral Ministries and Preaching, together with the teaching of Andi Cook, who taught alongside him at the seminary. It reflects not only academic study but decades of pastoral and seminary experience.
blocks.es_reference: Este curso proviene del currículo de adoración del Dr. Wayne Cook, quien sirvió once años como Profesor de Ministerios Pastorales y Predicación, junto con la enseñanza de Andi Cook, quien enseñó a su lado en el seminario. Refleja no solo el estudio académico sino décadas de experiencia pastoral y de seminario.

blocks.en: I. Ten Characteristics of True Worship
blocks.es_reference: I. Diez características de la adoración verdadera

blocks.en: Having defined worship, we now ask what true worship looks like. Worship can be done badly or well, falsely or truly, and Scripture gives us marks to test it by. Consider ten characteristics, each with an opposite that warns us when worship has gone wrong.
blocks.es_reference: Habiendo definido la adoración, ahora preguntamos cómo se ve la adoración verdadera. La adoración puede hacerse mal o bien, falsa o verdaderamente, y la Escritura nos da marcas para probarla. Considere diez características, cada una con un opuesto que nos advierte cuando la adoración se ha desviado.

blocks.en: First, worship is God-centered. Isaiah 6:1 says, "I saw the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up." The whole vision is fixed on God. The opposite is man-centered worship, where the focus quietly slides from God to ourselves, to our preferences, our feelings, our entertainment. Second, worship is reverent. There is a sense of awe before the holy God. The old English word "awful" once meant full of awe. The opposite is worship that is common, coarse, or profane, treating God as though He were just like us. Third, worship is corporate. It is the worship of the gathered body. Hebrews 10:25 commands us not to forsake "the assembling of ourselves together," and where two or three gather in His name, He is present. The opposite is the privatized faith that tries to meet God only at the lake or on the golf course.
blocks.es_reference: Primero, la adoración está centrada en Dios. Isaías 6:1 dice: "Vi al Señor sentado sobre un trono, alto y sublime." Toda la visión está fija en Dios. Lo opuesto es la adoración centrada en el hombre, donde el enfoque se desliza calladamente de Dios a nosotros mismos, a nuestras preferencias, nuestros sentimientos, nuestro entretenimiento. Segundo, la adoración es reverente. Hay un sentido de asombro ante el Dios santo. La antigua palabra inglesa "awful" una vez significó lleno de asombro. Lo opuesto es la adoración que es común, vulgar, o profana, tratando a Dios como si fuera igual a nosotros. Tercero, la adoración es corporativa. Es la adoración del cuerpo reunido. Hebreos 10:25 manda no dejar de "congregarnos," y donde dos o tres se reúnen en Su nombre, Él está presente. Lo opuesto es la fe privatizada que intenta encontrarse con Dios solo en el lago o en el campo de golf.

blocks.en: II. Humble, Spiritual, Free, and Joyous
blocks.es_reference: II. Humilde, espiritual, libre, y gozosa

blocks.en: Fourth, worship is humble. We cannot worship God with pride. At the burning bush God told Moses to remove his sandals, for the ground was holy. Isaiah, seeing the Lord, cried "Woe is me!" The proud Pharisee, by contrast, thanked God that he was not like other men, and went home unjustified. You cannot exalt God and self at the same moment. Fifth, worship is spiritual. Jesus said we must worship in spirit and in truth (John 4:24). True worship is guided by the Spirit of God; the opposite is fleshly worship, and it is entirely possible to pray and even preach in the flesh rather than in the Spirit.
blocks.es_reference: Cuarto, la adoración es humilde. No podemos adorar a Dios con orgullo. En la zarza ardiente Dios le dijo a Moisés que se quitara las sandalias, porque la tierra era santa. Isaías, al ver al Señor, clamó "¡Ay de mí!" El fariseo orgulloso, por contraste, agradeció a Dios no ser como los demás, y volvió a casa sin ser justificado. No se puede exaltar a Dios y a uno mismo en el mismo momento. Quinto, la adoración es espiritual. Jesús dijo que debemos adorar en espíritu y en verdad (Juan 4:24). La adoración verdadera es guiada por el Espíritu de Dios; lo opuesto es la adoración carnal, y es enteramente posible orar y aun predicar en la carne en lugar del Espíritu.

blocks.en: Sixth, worship is free. It must be planned, but it must always leave room for the movement of the Spirit. John 3:8 says the wind blows wherever it pleases. The opposite is rigid inflexibility that quenches the Spirit. I have been in services where the invitation went on for an hour and a half because the Spirit was moving, and no one dared cut it short. Seventh, worship is joyous. It is entirely possible to be consecrated and happy at the same time. D. L. Moody said he once walked into a church so cold you could have skated down the center aisle. Psalm 100:2 says, "Serve the Lord with gladness." The remaining characteristics, that worship is sincere, truthful, and orderly, all flow from these. Test your worship by these marks.
blocks.es_reference: Sexto, la adoración es libre. Debe ser planeada, pero siempre debe dejar lugar para el mover del Espíritu. Juan 3:8 dice que el viento sopla de donde quiere. Lo opuesto es la inflexibilidad rígida que apaga al Espíritu. He estado en servicios donde la invitación duró hora y media porque el Espíritu se movía, y nadie se atrevió a cortarla. Séptimo, la adoración es gozosa. Es enteramente posible estar consagrado y feliz al mismo tiempo. D. L. Moody dijo que una vez entró en una iglesia tan fría que se podría haber patinado por el pasillo central. El Salmo 100:2 dice: "Servid al Señor con alegría." Las características restantes, que la adoración es sincera, veraz, y ordenada, todas fluyen de estas. Pruebe su adoración por estas marcas.

blocks.en: III. Why Worship Matters: The Human Need
blocks.es_reference: III. Por qué importa la adoración: la necesidad humana

blocks.en: Why does worship matter so much? The first reason is that worship satisfies a deep-seated human need. Douglas Horton observed that man becomes a living soul and wants to worship. There is something instinctive in us that reaches out to worship something. That instinct can be diverted to idols, to money, to fame, to self, but it cannot be eliminated. Even the most hardened skeptic worships something. The soul was made for worship, and it is restless until it worships the God who made it.
blocks.es_reference: ¿Por qué importa tanto la adoración? La primera razón es que la adoración satisface una necesidad humana profunda. Douglas Horton observó que el hombre se vuelve un alma viviente y quiere adorar. Hay algo instintivo en nosotros que se extiende para adorar algo. Ese instinto puede ser desviado a los ídolos, al dinero, a la fama, a uno mismo, pero no puede ser eliminado. Aun el escéptico más endurecido adora algo. El alma fue hecha para la adoración, y está inquieta hasta que adora al Dios que la hizo.

blocks.en: The second reason is that worship builds fellowship. Horton said the entire task of the church is to extend into all of life the relationships already present in worship. We were made for fellowship, both with God and with one another. There is a practical pastoral truth here: unless a new person forms a real relationship with two or three people in his first months, he will not stay in the church. Worship is where those bonds are born.
blocks.es_reference: La segunda razón es que la adoración edifica la comunión. Horton dijo que toda la tarea de la iglesia es extender a toda la vida las relaciones ya presentes en la adoración. Fuimos hechos para la comunión, tanto con Dios como unos con otros. Hay una verdad pastoral práctica aquí: a menos que una persona nueva forme una relación real con dos o tres personas en sus primeros meses, no permanecerá en la iglesia. La adoración es donde nacen esos lazos.

blocks.en: IV. Why Worship Matters: It Pleases and Is Commanded by God
blocks.es_reference: IV. Por qué importa la adoración: agrada a Dios y es mandada por Él

blocks.en: The third reason worship matters is that it pleases God. God desires our fellowship the way a parent desires the company of a child. He is not indifferent to whether we come to Him; He delights in it. And the fourth reason is the simplest and the weightiest: worship is commanded. The greatest commandment is to love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul, strength, and mind. "Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy" is one of the Ten Commandments, not one of ten suggestions.
blocks.es_reference: La tercera razón por la que importa la adoración es que agrada a Dios. Dios desea nuestra comunión como un padre desea la compañía de un hijo. No es indiferente a si venimos a Él; se deleita en ello. Y la cuarta razón es la más sencilla y la más pesada: la adoración es mandada. El mayor mandamiento es amar al Señor tu Dios con todo tu corazón, alma, fuerza, y mente. "Acuérdate del día de reposo para santificarlo" es uno de los Diez Mandamientos, no una de diez sugerencias.

blocks.en: So worship is not an optional add-on to the Christian life. It answers the deepest need of the human soul, it builds the fellowship of the body, it pleases the God who made us, and it is commanded by Him. A church that takes worship lightly has misunderstood the most basic reason it exists.
blocks.es_reference: Así que la adoración no es un añadido opcional a la vida cristiana. Responde a la necesidad más profunda del alma humana, edifica la comunión del cuerpo, agrada al Dios que nos hizo, y es mandada por Él. Una iglesia que toma la adoración a la ligera ha malentendido la razón más básica por la que existe.

sa.prompt: The first characteristic of worship is that it is God-centered. Explain this using Isaiah 6:1, and identify its opposite.
sa.model: Worship is God-centered because Isaiah 6:1 fixes the entire vision on God, saying, 'I saw the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up.' The focus stays on who God is rather than drifting to us. The opposite is man-centered worship, where the focus quietly slides from God to our own preferences, feelings, and entertainment.

sa.prompt: Worship must be reverent. Explain the place of awe in worship and identify the opposite attitude.
sa.model: Reverent worship carries a sense of awe before the holy God — the old English word 'awful' once meant full of awe, capturing this proper posture. The opposite attitude is worship that becomes common, coarse, or profane, treating God as though He were just like us rather than the holy God He is.

sa.prompt: Worship is corporate. Explain this characteristic using Hebrews 10:25 and identify its opposite.
sa.model: Worship is corporate because it is the worship of the gathered body — Hebrews 10:25 commands believers not to forsake 'the assembling of ourselves together,' and where two or three gather in His name, He is present. The opposite is privatized faith that tries to meet God only alone, perhaps at the lake or on the golf course, apart from the gathered church.

sa.prompt: Worship must be humble. Using the examples of Moses, Isaiah, and the Pharisee, explain why pride is incompatible with worship.
sa.model: Pride is incompatible with worship because you cannot exalt God and self at the same moment. At the burning bush, God told Moses to remove his sandals because the ground was holy — an act of humility. Isaiah, seeing the Lord, cried 'Woe is me!' rather than boasting. By contrast, the proud Pharisee thanked God he was not like other men and went home unjustified, showing that pride blocks true worship even when the words sound religious.

sa.prompt: Worship must be spiritual. Explain what it means to worship in the Spirit, using John 4:23, and identify the opposite.
sa.model: To worship in the Spirit, as John 4:24 describes, means true worship is guided by the Spirit of God rather than merely produced by human effort or performance. The opposite is fleshly worship — it is entirely possible to pray and even preach in the flesh rather than in the Spirit, going through religious motions without genuine spiritual life behind them.

sa.prompt: Worship must be free. Explain how worship is both planned and open to the Spirit, using John 3:8.
sa.model: Worship must be planned, but it must always leave room for the movement of the Spirit, since John 3:8 says the wind blows wherever it pleases. Being free does not mean being unplanned; it means holding the plan loosely enough that the Spirit can still move within or beyond it, rather than quenching Him with rigid inflexibility.

sa.prompt: Worship should be joyous. Explain how holiness and joy belong together, and identify the opposite.
sa.model: Holiness and joy belong together because it is entirely possible to be consecrated and happy at the same time — Psalm 100:2 commands, 'Serve the Lord with gladness.' Genuine reverence does not require coldness. The opposite is worship so cold and lifeless that D. L. Moody described walking into a church so cold you could have skated down the center aisle.

sa.prompt: Worship satisfies a deep-seated human need to worship. Explain this, using Horton's observation about the soul.
sa.model: Worship satisfies a deep-seated human need because, as Douglas Horton observed, man becomes a living soul and wants to worship — there is something instinctive in us that reaches out to worship something. That instinct can be diverted to idols, money, fame, or self, but it cannot be eliminated; the soul was made for worship and is restless until it worships the God who made it.

sa.prompt: Worship builds fellowship. Explain this, using Horton's claim about the relationships present in worship.
sa.model: Worship builds fellowship because, as Horton claimed, the entire task of the church is to extend into all of life the relationships already present in worship — we were made for fellowship, both with God and with one another. There is a practical pastoral truth here: unless a new person forms a real relationship with two or three people in his first months, he will not stay in the church, and worship is where those bonds are born.

sa.prompt: Worship both pleases God and is commanded by God. Explain both, using the great commandment and the Sabbath command.
sa.model: Worship pleases God because He desires our fellowship the way a parent desires the company of a child, delighting in our coming to Him rather than being indifferent to it. Worship is also commanded: the greatest commandment is to love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul, strength, and mind, and 'Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy' is one of the Ten Commandments, not one of ten suggestions.
